prompt: The graph of $f(x) = x^2 + bx + 9$ touches the $x$-axis at exactly one point, and $b$ is positive. What is the value of $b$?
hint: Touching the $x$-axis at exactly one point means exactly one real zero.

hints.text: Touching the $x$-axis at exactly one point means exactly one real zero.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a known case: $x^2 + 4x + 4 = (x + 2)^2$ touches the axis once, and here $b = 4$ with $c = 4$ — note $b = 2\sqrt{c}$. Tangency means the trinomial is a perfect square.

learningObjective: Connect tangency to the x-axis with a zero discriminant.
explanation: A parabola touching the $x$-axis at exactly one point has a repeated root, so its discriminant is zero.
The problem states $b$ is positive, so $b = 6$. Check: $x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)^2$, tangent at $x = -3$ ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Read it as a perfect square
steps: One repeated root means the quadratic is a perfect square: $(x + k)^2 = x^2 + 2kx + k^2$.
Then $b = 2k = \pm 6$, and the positivity condition selects $6$. The condition on $b$ exists precisely because both signs are otherwise valid.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: b² = 36 tempts two errors: answering 36 itself, or forgetting the condition that picks between ±6.
Finish the square root, then apply the stated sign condition. The problem says b is positive precisely because both roots survive the algebra.
